slides.title: [Workshop title]
slides.notes: Start from the agreed delivery brief. Introduce the host, speakers and customer audience; explain what brought this group together. Names remain pending until supplied. This template is a storyboard scaffold, not a ready deck. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: Original host/presenter logo and workshop identity. Use supplied or official assets; do not invent marks.

slides.title: [What customers will build]
slides.body: [The actual user task, input and useful result]
slides.notes: Explain the customer problem with a concrete example from the agreed scenario. Identify what the published blueprint provides and what learners will implement. Describe unverified behavior as the intended result. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: Actual application screenshot or brief live demo showing the user journey. If the app is not running, mark capture pending; do not fabricate a successful screen.

slides.title: Today’s workshop
slides.notes: Replace placeholders with meaningful session sections and realistic times. Include setup, demonstrations, hands-on time, regrouping, breaks and Q&A within the actual slot. Record speaker handoffs and support roles. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: Readable session route, distinguishing presenter-led explanation from learner practice. Do not use a vendor list as the agenda.

slides.title: [Application name]: how the parts connect
slides.notes: Show the whole application before the first lab. Map every intended blueprint part and substitution. Start with the user input, then reveal runtime components and data paths; introduce tracing and evaluation as separate flows. Specify actual object groups and click order in the authored notes. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: Complete architecture using real product logos, role labels, directional arrows and boundaries. Show inputs, storage, model calls, UI output, tracing and evaluation only where the actual stack uses them.

slides.title: Before we start building
slides.notes: Use the access plan: distinguish prework from day-of setup, name who supplies access/credits and who helps attendees. Explain the fallback. Keep install commands and secrets in the appropriate local setup instructions. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: A simple environment orientation using the actual notebook, editor or console. Show the success indicator learners should check.

slides.title: Open the workshop on your laptop
slides.body: Keep the instructions beside your working environment.
slides.notes: Bind the real session URL before delivery. Introduce the destination after the application, agenda and architecture. Read it aloud and allow time to open it. No workshop QR code. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: A large, easy-to-type verified workshop URL. Until bound, show Workshop link pending.

slides.title: [Section number and name]
slides.body: [What this part adds to the application]
slides.notes: Repeat this section/concept/exercise/debrief pattern only for meaningful parts of the agreed module arc. State where the room is in the agenda and the next observable outcome. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: Return to the architecture with this section’s components highlighted; keep product labels consistent.

slides.title: [How this component handles the task]
slides.body: [Explain the actual input, action and output]
slides.notes: Use a worked example from the workshop. Explain the tool’s role and design choice, then demonstrate it. Plan Start, Click 1 and subsequent object reveals before rendering. Avoid generic definitions that do not explain this application. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: A focused request path plus real code, trace or output relevant to this component. Keep the complete architecture available for context.
reveals: [First meaningful step, with label and connector]

slides.title: [Build or change one concrete behavior]
slides.notes: Point to the exact lesson. Demonstrate the first action, then leave time to practice. Record duration, support route, a regroup cue and a recovery path. Full commands and solutions belong in the appropriate lesson/instructor files. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: A readable crop of the exercise entry point or expected checkpoint, sourced from the actual materials.

slides.title: [What changed in the application?]
slides.notes: Regroup the room. Explain why the observed behavior matters, discuss a common mistake and connect the outcome to the next section. Distinguish verified output from expected output. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: Real output or a before/after comparison, with only the relevant fields highlighted.

slides.title: [Run the completed application]
slides.notes: Return to the opening task and full architecture. Demonstrate what now works and explain remaining limits. For an evaluation module, show the dataset, checks and observed comparison; keep tracing distinct from evaluation. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: Actual application UI and relevant measured results. The architecture can highlight the path being demonstrated.

slides.title: [What learners can now build]
slides.body: [Completed capabilities and a practical next use case]
slides.notes: Recap only outcomes the workshop supports. Point to reusable repository files and explain what learners would adapt for their own use case. Avoid unsupported production-readiness claims. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: Return to the opening application or workflow with the completed capabilities labeled.

slides.title: Questions and next steps
slides.body: [A useful prompt about applying this workshop]
slides.notes: Use the reserved Q&A time. Record unanswered questions and requested follow-up without inventing answers. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: A quiet, readable slide with the relevant support or documentation route when known.

slides.title: Tell us how the workshop went
slides.body: What could you complete? Where did you get stuck? What should change?
slides.notes: Bind this session’s real survey destination. Allow time to respond. Generate a QR only for that verified URL and test the final slide; show the readable link too. [Sources] Replace with the actual workshop plan, product documentation or captured evidence. [/Sources]
slides.visual: Verified survey URL and matching QR with a quiet zone. Until configured, show Survey link pending and no QR.
